+Before the switch-over, raised by climb batch 28's rung A (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-28/RECORD.md`, "Items for the curator, and where each is in `PLAN.md`"):
+
+74. A.worker.1 and A.skeptic.4 of climb batch 28's rung A (row 933), a reserved point: the compiled transaction livelocks when an `atomic` block reads a variable it wrote, then commits a nested `atomic` block and reads again, since its read of its own write enters the read set and the next read validates it against the committed value; the compiled array store shares the path once arrays run compiled. Its repair is a change of the compiled transaction beyond shape (ii): which rung takes it, and does it hold any switch-over step? No default on record. Evidence: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:212-228`; row 933's program, exit 124 under `timeout 30` at the base and on the rung.
+
+### Climb batch 28, listed for his review
+
+The items for him that climb batch 28 (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md`, rungs V, R, A, K, H, S and T landed of seven, phase 4's sixth batch: the integer conversions, the reader side, the arrays' store, the checker's partial order, the run time's threads, `System`'s natives and `args`, and the code generator's api trait) left (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-28/RECORD.md`, "Items for the curator, and where each is in `PLAN.md`").
+
+- V.worker.1 and V.skeptic.1 of climb batch 28's rung V: should QuickCheck's `genZZ.perturb` keep the low 64 bits of a `ZZ` beyond `ZZ64` (`signed((obj BITAND 18446744073709551615).asNN64)`) until row 431's right-shift fix, as P-161's "with their values unchanged" reads, instead of raising `IntegerOverflow` on `.asZZ64`, which the review's option 6 names for this line? Default: `.asZZ64`, as landed; no gated run reaches such a value under walk (row 387). Evidence: `Library/QuickCheck.fss:322`; row 431; old 'perturb 2^70+7: 1001751898', new 'perturb 2^70+7: IntegerOverflow' (`compile-ladder/rung-integer-conversions/SKEPTIC.md`).
+- V.worker.2 and V.skeptic.2 of climb batch 28's rung V: `ZZ`'s `asZZ64` and `asNN64` bind two new helpers, departing from fork V1's default of no Java beyond its three pairs, since `ZZ` has no low-bits form to wrap after its `narrow` and `widen` went; P-162 supports new helpers for carried types. Default: as landed. Evidence: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.java:146-157`; `coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:396`.
+- R.worker.1, R.skeptic.1 and H.skeptic.1 of climb batch 28's rungs R and H (row 930), a reserved point: on the compiled path no `catch` saw a helper's raise of `IOFailure` or `FileNotFoundException`, since `Utility.makeFortressException(name, msg)` sought a constructor at `java.lang.String`, which the prelude's exception lacks. Rung R, whose brief reserved an edit of a run-time class, asked which change takes the repair, a run-time rung before N5 or N5; rung H, whose brief named neither, repaired it, since its own `FailCalled` test needs it and `basic/expressions/try.tex`, "Try Expressions", settles it, so the 13 compiled raises with a message reach a `catch`. Default: keep H's repair, as landed; the gather promoted R's pair to `FileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled` and closed row 930 by H's commit. Way not taken: revert it and build `FailCalled` by reflection in `runtime.java`, which leaves those raises uncatchable. Evidence: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:28-31`; `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FileOpsRaiseCaughtCompiled.fss`; `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/HelperRaiseMessageCompiled.fss`; `coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:544`, `:546`, `:673-675`.
+- R.judge.1 of climb batch 28's rung R: `FileWriteStream`'s write of a string that is not flat makes one write and no flush, where `Writer`'s flushes after it and fork R2 says "as Writer's are". Option 1, as landed: no flush, which keeps the file stream's buffering, so its other writes behave as before. Option 2: a flush after it, as `Writer` and the team's `Writer` did, one line, so a rope's write would flush where a flat string's does not. Lines stay whole either way. Default: option 1, as landed. Evidence: `Library/File.fss:57`; `Library/Writer.fss:32-35`; `coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:406`; `compile-ladder/rung-io-reader/JUDGE.md`.

## Revival changes, for the skill writer

### V (`rung-integer-conversions`, `45868b113`)

**The change.** The team's walk library declared `narrow` and `widen` on ZZ, bound to glue that keeps the low 32 and 64 bits (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1150-1154 at 157323e51, the comment "This routine, named for consistency, converts to a ZZ64"), and at 157323e51 the library declared each of narrow, widen, signed, unsigned and big on some of the five integer types only, and no checked conversion on them: the team's one, ZZ64's narrow, which ended the run with "Overflow of ZZ32", the revival made keep the low 32 bits (P-72; explorations/reviews/integer-conversions-2026-11-06.md, "3.2 The library as the team wrote it"); the team's later compiler library declares the checked getter asZZ32 of ZZ64 (`jLongOverflowingToInt`, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:581) and the four bitsAs getters (:583, :668, :758, :824); the Working Draft of February 2011 names none of these conversions. The tree now gives each of ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32, NN64 and ZZ the getters asZZ32, asZZ64, asNN32, asNN64 and asZZ, which keep the value and raise IntegerOverflow where it does not fit; the fixed widths the bitsAs getters; narrow, widen, signed, unsigned and big on every type where each applies, keeping the bits; and ZZ no narrow or widen (tests/IntegerConversionsWalk.fss; under walk `narrow(z)` of a ZZ fails 'Failed to find any matching overload'). The numeral type IntLiteral's conversions, strings, = and cmp are Fortress over its asZZ (tests/IntLiteralTextWalk.fss). The reason, as evidence: under the team's walk library, `widen` of the ZZ 2^63 answered 'widen: -9223372036854775808' and `narrow` of the ZZ 2^32+5 'narrow: 5'; `widen` of the NN64 2^64-1 went through ZZ's `widen` by coercion and answered 'widen: -1 : ZZ64'; and `narrow` of the NN32 2^32-1 stopped with 'Ambiguous coercion, args = (4294967295: NN32)' (four probes run on the old code; on the tree they answer 'Failed to find any matching overload', the same, '18446744073709551615 : NN64' and 'narrow: 4294967295'). The team's later compiler library binds its plain asZZ32 to the native that raises (ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:581), and the specification says "For integer results, overflow throws an IntegerOverflow." (Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:155).

**Provenance.** P-161, option 6 of explorations/reviews/integer-conversions-2026-11-06.md; P-169 for IntLiteral's 8; P-162 for ZZ32's big; the batch record's forks V1 to V6, with V1 departed from for ZZ's asZZ64 and asNN64. Climb batch 28, rung V.

### R (`rung-io-reader`, `71d1018d1`)

**The change.** The team's walk library declared `File` and `Reader` as native components whose `FileReadStream`, `FileWriteStream`, `Reader` and `stdIn` are glue objects (base `Library/File.fss:12-96`, `Library/Reader.fss:12-61`): `FileWriteStream` extends only `FileStream` and has no `flush` though its api declares one (base `Library/File.fsi:102`, `:131`), so a rope written to it and its `flush()` stop the run; a missing file, a read after `consume` and a read after `close` stop the run with errors that no `catch` sees ('FileNotFound: …', `interpreter/glue/prim/FileReadStream.java:44`; 'Performed operation on consumed FileReadStream …', `:70`; 'Read IOException on <Read handle to …>', `:79-89`). The tree now declares `object FileReadStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)`, `object FileWriteStream(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedWriter) extends { FileStream, WriteStream }` and `object Reader(fileName: String, under: JavaBufferedReader)`, each over a Java-backed value in its field, beside one-argument factories of the old names (`Library/File.fsi:17-19`, `:99-101`; `Library/Reader.fsi:17-19`); `FileWriteStream` takes a rope and flushes; a missing file raises `FileNotFoundException`, a read after `consume` and an I/O error `IOFailure`, both of which a `catch` sees under walk; after `close`, reads answer the end's values (`""`, `char(0)`, -1) and `ready` raises `IOFailure`. Shown by `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperReaderWalk.fss`. The reason: walk's glue classes take walk's values, so the compiled code cannot call them, and every file a program reads goes through these objects (`explorations/run-c4/src/FlatData.fss:69-86`); the team's own later `FileReadStream` holds a Java reader in a field (`ProjectFortress/BirdyLib/File.fss:20-34`), and the team's helpers already raise the exceptions (`nativeHelpers/fileOps.java:37`, `compiler/runtimeValues/FortressBufferedReader.java:119-121`). The answers after `close` are the team's compiled reader's (`FortressBufferedReader.java:39`, `:56`, `:73`), which returns the end's values once `eof` is set.

**Provenance.** P-164 (option (b) of `explorations/reviews/io-objects-carrier-2026-11-06.md`), with review-queue item 373 for `FileWriteStream`, and forks R1 to R7 of `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md` at their defaults (R6 for the exceptions, item 384 at its default: they carry no message); climb batch 28, rung R.

### A (`rung-array-store`, `a6c884cd8`)

**The change.**

- The team's `NativeArray` was a native component whose three objects were walk's native objects over glue classes: `native component NativeArray` and `get(i:ZZ32):T = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.PrimitiveArray$get")` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss:12-50` at 157323e5), so walk alone could run an array. The tree now has a plain `component NativeArray` whose `PrimitiveArray` and `PrimImmutableArray` hold a `JavaArrayStore` of `FortressLibrary` in a field and read `cast[\T\](mem.get(i))`, and whose `PrimImmutableRR64Array` holds a `JavaRR64ArrayStore`; the stores bind helpers that the compiled path runs over an `Object[]` and a `double[]`, and that walk answers with its own `AtomicArray` and `double[]`. Tests: `tests/ArrayStoreWalk.fss`, `compiler/runtimeValues/ArrayStoreJUTest.java`. Reason: a body left on glue compiles to the library's own `builtinPrimitive`, whose body is `fail` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:34-35`), so every array, vector, varargs list and `args` of a compiled program would raise.
- The team's compiled transaction tracked only `MutableFValue` cells (`Hashtable<MutableFValue, Any> reads`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:27-28` at 157323e5). It now also tracks an element of an `Object[]` by its array and its index, `TXReadSlot` and `TXWriteSlot` (`Transaction.java:25-79`, `:203-231`, `:292-297`). Test: `ArrayStoreJUTest`, four tasks adding into one element inside `atomic`, exact. Reason: an array's elements have no cell each in an `Object[]` store, and a write inside `atomic` must be part of the transaction (`Specification/basic/memory-model.tex:68-75`).
- The team's walk store of an immutable array overwrote an element on a second initialisation (`interpreter/glue/prim/PrimImmutableArray.java:73-82` at 157323e5: `contents[i] = v; return (old == null)`), while a mutable array's ignored it (`AtomicArray.java:60-65`). Both arrays now share one store, and both ignore it: `immutableArray[\ZZ32\](2).fill(3).fill(4)` holds `3 3`. Test: `tests/ArrayInitOnceWalk.fss`. Reason: one store for both arrays; the api asks for one initialisation and an error on a second (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1510-1515`), which neither store signals.
- The team's `NativeArray` api declared `PrimitiveArray` and `PrimImmutableArray` only (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fsi:14-16` at 157323e5); it now also declares `PrimImmutableRR64Array` (`:18`), which a program can make; no factory chooses it. Test: `tests/ArrayStoreRR64Walk.fss`. Reason: base 'Function PrimImmutableRR64Array is not defined.'

**Provenance.** P-169 (the arrays' 7 on compiled helpers that walk's loader answers with its own operations, P-167's device; P-164's pattern of a Java-backed trait); the judgement's Q2, answered (ii), the slot API (review-queue item 407); the batch's forks A1 to A7 (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:413-421`), A7 for the second initialisation; climb batch 28, rung A.

### K (`rung-checker-partial-order`, `a3eba5067`)

Revival change: none. The change repairs a crash of the team's checker, which sorted by a partial order with a sort that needs a total one; on the one library it keeps every result of the checker, and a tie's arrow is a candidate that no other applicable candidate is more specific than, the set from which `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:309-311` lets the run time choose; which of them the checker takes statically the specification does not fix (row 935). No rule of the language, and nothing walk, the library or the specification says, changes.

### H (`rung-runtime-threads`, `70c26e3fd`)

**The change.** The team's library bound `Thread`'s `val`, `wait`, `ready` and `stop` and `abort` to walk's glue classes (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:775-786` at 157323e5) and `printTaskTrace` to `StringPrim$PrintTaskTrace` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4625` at 157323e5), which only walk runs, and the team's compiled run time ended every helper raise that carries a message in `FortressImplementationError`, since `Utility.makeFortressException` looked up a constructor over `java.lang.String` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:30` at 157323e5). The tree now binds the six to helpers that the compiled path runs: compiled, `abort()` abandons and reruns an `atomic` block that is not nested in another (in a nested one the outer block reruns, row 937, `compiler_tests/XXXNestedAtomicAbortCompiled`) and does nothing outside one, `printTaskTrace()` prints one line `Task: <class>` for each task from the current one to the program's own, and `Thread`'s four raise `FailCalled` "spawn is not compiled yet"; walk does as before (`tests/RuntimeOwnOperationsWalk`, `compiler_tests/RuntimeOwnOperationsCompiled`). A compiled helper's raise with a message now raises the named exception, which a `catch` sees (`compiler_tests/HelperRaiseMessageCompiled`). The reason: a body left on glue compiles to the library's own `builtinPrimitive`, which fails; the specification's `abort` (`Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/transactions.tex:15-21`); and the measured failure on the base, `FortressImplementationError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin$FileNotFoundException.<init>(java.lang.String)`. A test of `abort` counts its tries by the clock, since a counter written inside the block is rolled back with the try.

**Provenance.** P-169's threads, `abort` and task trace (Q1 of the natives device review, yes), by P-167's device, with P-162's pair for `val`; the batch record's forks H1 to H4 at their defaults; the repair of `Utility` is the rung's, a point to report. Climb batch 28, rung H.

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`; for a noted block, no `--note`), a correction that
names no block or more than one, two blocks for one entry in one call.
Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the record file and its
history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'
